recent_posts.title: How agentic AI workflows made a codebase-wide Ruby refactor feasible
recent_posts.summary: A Gusto engineer shares how agentic AI workflows made a large-scale Ruby codebase refactor feasible by replacing OpenStruct with faster alternatives. The key insight wasn't AI's code generation speed but the ability to cheaply iterate on the decomposition strategy itself. Initial attempts using one PR per module caused reviewer fatigue; grouping PRs by team ownership solved the bottleneck. Claude Code was used to build a reusable skill that scans for deprecated patterns, groups changes by team, generates replacements, and measures performance. A two-agent setup ran refactoring and performance benchmarking in parallel using git worktrees, producing concrete metrics (25–39x faster instantiation, 90%+ memory reduction) that justified the work. A GitHub issue served as a living dashboard and shared memory between sessions.

recent_posts.title: Great Work Partners Keep You on Your Toes
recent_posts.summary: Reflecting on what makes work partnerships truly effective, the key insight is that the best collaborators introduce productive friction rather than removing it. Three behaviors define these partners: they stop the team to question assumptions (like catching a $2M impact estimate that was actually $15K), they take ownership without waiting for perfect alignment, and they know when 'good enough' is the right call. Over time, working with such people internalizes their critical thinking habits, making you a better engineer and decision-maker.

recent_posts.title: Universal Document Processing at Gusto: From One-Off Parsers to a Self-Service Platform
recent_posts.summary: Gusto's engineering team describes how they replaced fragile, one-off document parsers with a Universal Document Processing (UDP) platform. Facing millions of documents per year across payroll, benefits, and compliance workflows, they decomposed the problem into five composable API-backed stages: ingestion, classification, extraction, validation, and mapping. AI is used as a model-agnostic abstraction layer rather than a hard dependency, with confidence scores and fallback routing as first-class concepts. The result is a self-service platform where teams can onboard new document types through configuration rather than code, business users own mapping logic, and the system gracefully handles failures. Key lessons include prioritizing domain understanding over model selection, investing in confidence calibration, and treating the mapping layer as a high-complexity concern.

recent_posts.title: The Journey to a Safer Frontend: Why We Removed React.FC
recent_posts.summary: Gusto Engineering removed React.FC from their codebase after discovering it silently weakened TypeScript's type checking. The utility type allowed invalid default props, hid unused props, and broke generic type inference. Through automated codemods, they migrated over 5,000 files to explicit prop typing with clear return types, uncovering dozens of hidden bugs in the process. The change improved type safety, code predictability, and was enforced going forward with ESLint rules.

recent_posts.title: It Takes a Village: Building Gusto’s First AI Risk Agent
recent_posts.summary: Building an AI risk agent at Gusto required close collaboration between engineers and domain experts, not just technical implementation. The team discovered that success came from tight feedback loops with operations specialists who understood the nuances of risk assessment, pragmatic architectural decisions favoring learning over purity, and treating prompts like code specifications. The resulting system reduced manual reviews by 70% and achieved 6x faster approval times by combining AI automation with human oversight safeguards.

recent_posts.title: Three productivity habits for software engineers
recent_posts.summary: Practical strategies for improving developer productivity through three core habits: staying unblocked by working on tasks in parallel and maintaining a breadth-first approach, reducing debugging time by building mental maps of codebases and investing in proper logging, and maximizing efficiency by mastering versatile tools and automating repetitive tasks with AI assistance.

recent_posts.title: Celebrating Impact: Voices of Long-Tenured Gusties
recent_posts.summary: Long-tenured engineers at Gusto share their experiences working at the payroll and HR software company for 5-10 years. They discuss what attracted them to the company, how they've grown professionally, and the impact of their work on customers. Key themes include solving complex payroll problems, maintaining customer-centric focus, collaborative culture, and the technical challenges of building scalable financial software. The engineers highlight memorable moments like implementing Employee Retention Credit during the pandemic and how the company has evolved while maintaining its core mission.

recent_posts.title: From Practice to Pitch: A Tech Intern’s Guide to Interviewing
recent_posts.summary: A tech intern shares insights on approaching technical interviews by drawing parallels to competitive sports. The guide emphasizes preparation through coding practice, maintaining proper mindset on interview day, demonstrating collaboration skills, evaluating company culture, and learning from each interview experience. Key advice includes treating interviews as collaborative problem-solving sessions rather than solo performances, prioritizing rest and self-care before interviews, and focusing on communication and teamwork alongside technical skills.

recent_posts.title: Building Strong Teams: Lessons from Beavers for Tech Leads
recent_posts.summary: Tech leads should shift from micromanaging every detail (octopus approach) to empowering team members with full ownership of subdomains (beaver approach). This means delegating not just execution but also planning, stakeholder management, and decision-making within appropriate scopes. The key is matching ownership levels to individual skills and providing guidance on how to make decisions rather than what decisions to make. This approach reduces bottlenecks, increases team engagement, and develops future leaders while allowing tech leads to focus on high-level coordination and system design.

recent_posts.title: Distinguishing necessary complexity from pointless code verbosity
recent_posts.summary: Chesterton's Fence principle teaches developers to understand the purpose of seemingly unnecessary code before removing it, as it may protect against non-obvious bugs. However, not all complex code serves a purpose - 'False Fences' are unnecessary complexity that should be removed. The key is distinguishing between protective code and pointless verbosity through proper investigation, documentation, and following coding best practices like consistency, language idioms, and clear commenting.

top_posts.title: How We Made Payments Packaging 81 Times Faster
top_posts.summary: Gusto's Payments Engineering team faced challenges with their payments packaging process due to anticipated volume and limitations. They re-architected the process using a map reduce architecture for parallelism. They also implemented the ACH Engine to optimize packaging based on submission dates and created a locking mechanism to prevent race conditions. The process was further optimized to increase the file limit for higher throughput.
